issues.description: The solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and the corresponding Pig/Seal implementations expect an int parameter), but the problem statement/UML and the template expect a no-argument messageOnRide() that returns a String. The template's Main (commented example) calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. This parameter mismatch between specification/template and the solution will confuse students about the method signature they should implement and prevents direct correspondence with the UML and example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the specification by updating Rideable.messageOnRide to a no-argument method (String messageOnRide()) and adjust Pig/Seal implementations to return strings like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) if the speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement/UML and the template Main example to include the int speed parameter and examples showing how to call messageOnRide(speed). Option A is recommended to align with the current UML and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Rideable.messageOnRide() that returns a String like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implementations use the speed parameter. This signature mismatch (same conceptual method with different parameters) will confuse students: the provided Main template calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments, the UML and instructions describe a no-arg method, yet the solution requires an int argument and formats the return including speed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use the no-argument signature: messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" and update Pig/Seal implementations accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement and template to declare and call messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the expected return format. Aligning all three (problem, template, solution) to the same method signature will remove the mapping confusion.
